other.content: 1996 examination report indicates: “There is a stamp on the two central vertical stretcher bars in dark pink ink; “WARP PROOF TREATED ANCO BILT IS WELL BUILT ANCO INC., GLENDALE, N.Y.” Also written in pencil are the inscriptions, lower right; “Leo Robinson, 60 x 80”; lower left, “L-R-R-1” and finally upper right, “59 E 54 Apt. 84” (O’Keefe’s N.Y. address according to Barbara Lynes…” (Source: NGA, 2025)

cr_data.provenance: The artist [1887-1986]; her estate; bequest 1987 to NGA. (Source: NGA, 2025)
remarks_1999: Not recorded Downtown Gallery Archive. Whitney Archive in 1969 indicates [by Lloyd Goodrich], "Notes on works seen in Abiquiú, 12/1969: 'Sky Above White Clouds I' 1962 60 x 80. White below, yellow-green along horizon, then pinkish, then blue above. O'K. prefers to #2 and 3 x x x." (By this I meant the two earliest broken–cloud sky ptgs, which I numbered '2' and '3') Marked x for ex(cellent). As I remember it, this painting was hanging in O'Keeffe's living room. I remember it as a solid sky cover of cloud (not broken clouds), and I think with a diagonal darkish track across the clouds, like the trail of a plane." Written 3/70/69. "Doris Bry says no 4/8/70." Goodrich's description matches cat. no. 1483, which explains Doris Bry comment. 59 E 54 is the address of the apartment O'Keeffe and Stieglitz moved into in 1942. Stretcher inscription 2 names maker of stretcher. Abiquiú Notebooks, Whitney Archive after 1969 date 1962. Backing inscription dates 1961. (Source: Lynes, 1999)

description: A large white cloud fills the lower three-quarters of the canvas. The sky glows yellow where it meets the white rectangle, then transitions to blue at the top of the work.
